title: Why We Chose a Credit-Based Model for VideoAI
body_html:
Why This Matters Right Now

The broadcast industry is under constant pressure to deliver high-quality content faster and more efficiently. One of the key bottlenecks in this process is the manual tagging and metadata creation for video assets. This is where AI-powered video tagging comes into play, and the recent adoption of a credit-based model for VideoAI by Pond5 is a significant development. By leveraging AI inference pipelines, broadcast engineers and operations leads can optimize their workflows, reducing the time and cost associated with manual tagging and metadata creation. This, in turn, enables faster and more efficient content delivery, which is critical in today's fast-paced media landscape. The ability to automatically generate high-quality metadata is a game-changer for broadcast operations. It enables more efficient search and retrieval of video assets, which is essential for newsrooms, live production environments, and post-production workflows. Moreover, the use of AI-powered video tagging can also improve the accuracy and consistency of metadata, which is critical for ensuring that content is properly cataloged and easily accessible. This is particularly important in cloud-based workflows, where the ability to quickly and easily search and retrieve assets is essential for efficient content delivery. The adoption of a credit-based model for VideoAI is also significant because it provides a more flexible and scalable solution for broadcast operations. By allowing users to purchase credits that can be used to process video assets, Pond5 is providing a more cost-effective and efficient solution for broadcast engineers and operations leads. This is particularly important in today's cloud-based workflows, where the ability to quickly and easily scale up or down to meet changing demand is critical.

Under the Hood: How It Actually Works

The credit-based model for VideoAI is built on top of AI inference pipelines that are designed to optimize the processing of video assets. These pipelines use machine learning algorithms to analyze video content and generate high-quality metadata, including tags, descriptions, and other relevant information. The use of AI-powered video tagging enables broadcast operations to automate the metadata creation process, reducing the time and cost associated with manual tagging. The AI inference pipelines are designed to work with a variety of video formats and codecs, including those used in live production and post-production environments. The credit-based model for VideoAI also involves the use of JPEG XS compression, which is a visually lossless compression standard that provides minimal latency. This is significant because it enables the efficient transport of high-quality video signals over IP networks, using standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS. The use of JPEG XS compression reduces the bitrate required for transmitting high-quality video signals, resulting in lower transmission costs and simplified signal routing. This is particularly important in live production environments, where the ability to quickly and easily transport high-quality video signals is critical. The AI inference pipelines used in the credit-based model for VideoAI are designed to work with a variety of metadata schema, including Dublin Core, EBUCore, and IPTC. This enables broadcast operations to generate high-quality metadata that is consistent with industry standards, making it easier to search and retrieve video assets. The use of AI-powered video tagging also enables the generation of confidence scores, which provide a measure of the accuracy and reliability of the metadata generated by the AI algorithms.

What This Looks Like in a Real Broadcast Operation

In a real broadcast operation, the credit-based model for VideoAI can be used to automate the metadata creation process for video assets. For example, in a newsroom environment, AI-powered video tagging can be used to quickly and easily generate metadata for incoming video feeds, enabling faster and more efficient search and retrieval of assets. This can be particularly useful in breaking news situations, where the ability to quickly and easily access and retrieve video assets is critical. In a live production environment, the credit-based model for VideoAI can be used to optimize the transport of high-quality video signals over IP networks. The use of JPEG XS compression enables the efficient transport of video signals, reducing the bitrate required and resulting in lower transmission costs. This can be particularly useful in situations where high-quality video signals need to be transported over long distances, such as in remote production environments. The credit-based model for VideoAI can also be used in post-production environments to automate the metadata creation process for video assets. For example, AI-powered video tagging can be used to generate metadata for video assets during the ingest process, enabling faster and more efficient search and retrieval of assets during the editing process. This can be particularly useful in situations where large amounts of video footage need to be ingested and cataloged, such as in documentary or reality TV production.

The Practical Impact: Cost, Speed, and Scale

The credit-based model for VideoAI has a number of practical implications for broadcast operations. One of the most significant is the reduction in cost associated with manual tagging and metadata creation. By automating the metadata creation process, broadcast operations can reduce the time and cost associated with manual tagging, enabling faster and more efficient content delivery. This can be particularly useful in situations where large amounts of video footage need to be ingested and cataloged, such as in newsroom or live production environments. The use of AI-powered video tagging also enables faster and more efficient search and retrieval of video assets. This can be particularly useful in situations where quick access to video assets is critical, such as in breaking news situations or live production environments. The ability to quickly and easily search and retrieve video assets can also enable more efficient content delivery, which is critical in today's fast-paced media landscape. The credit-based model for VideoAI also enables more efficient scaling of broadcast operations. By providing a flexible and scalable solution for metadata creation, Pond5 is enabling broadcast operations to quickly and easily scale up or down to meet changing demand. This can be particularly useful in cloud-based workflows, where the ability to quickly and easily scale up or down is critical for efficient content delivery.

The Reality Check

While the credit-based model for VideoAI is a significant development, there are still a number of challenges and limitations that need to be considered. One of the most significant is the accuracy and reliability of the metadata generated by the AI algorithms. While AI-powered video tagging can generate high-quality metadata, there is still a risk of errors or inconsistencies, particularly in situations where the video content is complex or ambiguous. Another challenge is the integration of the credit-based model for VideoAI with existing broadcast systems and workflows. While the use of standards such as ST 2110 and NMOS can enable efficient transport of video signals, there may still be challenges in integrating the AI-powered video tagging with existing metadata schema and workflows. This can be particularly challenging in situations where there are multiple vendors and systems involved, such as in live production or post-production environments.
